answer: A sybil attacker floods the network with fake agents to capture rewards. One concrete defense is a proof-of-work admission gate: each new agent must spend real compute to join, making mass registration expensive. Like timber that must be seasoned before building, genuine agents prove themselves over time. A trusted haven for verified identities acts as a harbor for honest work, while each attestation adds weight that sybils cannot cheaply replicate. The economic cost of faking history makes attacks unprofitable.
